title: Warming richness deficits had no clear linear growth in two Cedar Creek planting groups in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether recorded warming richness deficits grew after the first harvest in two Cedar Creek planting groups. We used 432 annual records from nine whole plots per group in 2017-2022. Paired linear time slopes of heated-minus-control richness were -0.0063 species per year in four-species plantings and +0.0254 in 16-species plantings. Two-test adjusted plot intervals were -0.0935 to +0.0808 and -0.1341 to +0.1849. All separate water and period checks were uncertain. A lower mean richness under warming does not by itself show a growing deficit after the first harvest. Constant additive counting offsets cancel from the slope; changing offsets can reverse these small point estimates. This is a follow-up with shared observations, not independent regional replication. Moving harvest strips, nine plots per group, no pretreatment record, one site and a linear trend model limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes, a figure and independent arithmetic checks are included. Raw source records stay external.

display.caption: Annual mean heat contrasts and paired linear trend estimates. Bars are 97.5% t intervals across nine whole plots in each group. The two primary intervals give at least 95% joint coverage under the stated plot model.
